name: What should be prioritized when restoring a foreclosed property?

mainEntity.name: What should be prioritized when restoring a foreclosed property?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restoring a neglected or foreclosed home requires addressing structural soundness, utility systems, and cosmetic degradation in a strict priority order. The first step is assessing framing stability, roof leaks, subfloor integrity, and outdated or non-functioning electrical and plumbing systems. Cosmetic improvements—such as interior paint, new kitchen cabinetry, or tile installation—should never begin until underlying moisture issues and framing defects are fully corrected. In foreclosed rehabs, working with a hands-on general contractor who handles framing, drywall, and finish carpentry while coordinating trade specialists streamlines the project, preventing cosmetic work from being ruined by overlooked mechanical or moisture problems.
acceptedAnswer.description: Prioritize structural repairs, framing integrity, moisture barriers, and mechanical utilities first. Install drywall, tile, cabinetry, and interior paint only after the home is sound.
